name: Caesar Augustus
overview: Caesar Augustus was the Roman ruler at the time of Jesus' incarnation, as noted in Luke 2:1. He was a male figure of authority during this pivotal moment in salvation history. There are no additional tribal or personal notes recorded about him in Scripture beyond his role at this time.
namesAndTitles: The title 'Caesar Augustus' is the only name recorded for this person and does not have a specified meaning given in the biblical text. It identifies him as the Roman emperor during the birth of Christ, as referenced in Luke 2:1.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Caesar Augustus beyond what is indicated by his unique role at the time of Jesus' birth. There are no listed relationships in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Caesar Augustus is significant in the biblical narrative because his decree led to the census that brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, fulfilling the Messianic prophecy of the Messiah's birthplace. His political authority set the stage for the incarnation of Jesus Christ, demonstrating God's sovereign use of earthly rulers to accomplish divine purposes.
